mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces equity discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals labor market weakness that may prompt central bank intervention, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as investors anticipate policy support.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and rise in CPI inflation signals a central bank's attempt to combat inflation with rate cuts, which typically boosts equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of FEDFUNDS decline and CPIAUCSL rise fails to predict positive returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market expansion regime (HOUST > 1200 thousand units), rising home construction activity signals strong consumer demand and economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 1200, or the average return in the housing boom regime is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production falls below 100 (index base 2017=100), it indicates a contraction in manufacturing activity that typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the average return in contraction periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising residential sales volume (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending and economic activity, which consistently drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy expands.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS rises, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a robust labor market, which typically boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS rise and UNRATE decline fails to predict positive returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL annualized inflation > 2.5%), central bank tightening expectations lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as higher discount rates reduce equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL annualized inflation > 2.5, or the average return in high inflation periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).
